fields.sections.0.h: 2020 React Native Adoption: Successful, but Underlying Conditions Changed
fields.sections.1.h: Rapid LLM Advancement Inverts the Cost Structure
fields.sections.3.h: Open Source Library Handover: Responsible Transition with Community
fields.sections.4.h: Gradual Migration vs. Full Rebuild—Why the Latter Was Chosen
fields.sections.5.h: Helix System: Converting AI-Generated Code into Shipping Product
fields.sections.6.h: Simulator Bottleneck Solved: Headless Architecture and CLI-Based Feedback
fields.sections.7.h: What Migration Means: Rebuild, But No Compromise on Quality
fields.sections.8.h: Conditional Justification of Technology Choices, and Gratitude to the Ecosystem
fields.sections.0.ko: In 2020, Shopify's adoption of React Native allowed the company to implement features once and deploy to both platforms, saving substantial engineering time. At the same time, developers without mobile backgrounds could now participate in app development, and the burden of keeping features in sync across platforms was significantly reduced. Early this year, Shopify publicly stated that React Native had a bright future, but shortly afterward, the performance of coding AI models improved dramatically, causing the core assumptions behind that original decision to unravel. The company decided to re-evaluate its technology stack from scratch.
fields.sections.1.ko: Since 2021, Shopify has used LLMs in software development, initially limiting them to assisting with individual feature implementation and bug fixes. However, as models improved, by late 2025 they raised a fundamental question: whether implementing the same feature on two platforms really amounts to twice the work. The company prototyped rebuilding core portions of its largest apps in Swift and Kotlin, with results that far exceeded expectations. Agents could implement Android features by referencing the iOS version and vice versa, while platform synchronization costs dropped significantly.
fields.sections.2.ko: The cost of maintaining and managing two separate platforms remains, but as agents automated substantial portions of implementation, translation, testing, and code review work, this ceased to be the decisive factor it was in 2020. While React Native apps can be fast, Native development has regained its fundamental advantages: closer alignment with platform capabilities and official tools, and fewer intermediate framework and dependency layers. To ensure this transition happens cleanly, the company is also publicly redefining how it manages open source libraries it contributed to the React Native ecosystem.
fields.sections.3.ko: Shopify has maintained several important libraries in the React Native ecosystem, including FlashList, which sees approximately 2 million downloads per week. The company will continue sponsorship through the end of 2026, transferring core libraries to new maintainers and archiving lower-priority ones like Restyle to allow the community to fork freely. This transition is gradual, with an emphasis on giving library users sufficient time to prepare.
fields.sections.4.ko: Shopify considered two approaches: partially migrating the existing React Native app (gradual) or rebuilding it completely (full rebuild), ultimately choosing the latter. When previously migrating to React Native, the company used a modify-in-place approach, which took years. This time, agents can build features in Swift and Kotlin by referencing the React Native version, design from scratch without constraints, and prototypes complete far faster than before. The Shop app was already fully rebuilt as a Native app and shipped to the app store in 12 weeks, and the Shopify app—which has over 300 screens—is currently underway.
fields.sections.5.ko: Attempts to feed React Native code directly to agents for one-shot Native conversion failed, producing unmaintainable code. To solve this problem, Shopify built a system called Helix, which does not expect the first attempt to be perfect but instead runs iterative loops through small checkpoints. When a developer specifies a particular screen, Helix reads the React Native code and proposes small, reviewable units of work (checkpoints); each is proven by tests, undergoes visual review, and passes through two opposing reviewers before commit. As feedback accumulates across reviews, the agent's autonomy increases as migration progresses.
fields.sections.6.ko: Agents controlling the simulator created a severe bottleneck. Code changes took seconds, but verifying test results took minutes. To address this, Shopify designed the app architecture with both humans and agents in mind, completely separating business logic from the UI to run headlessly on the desktop. Through the CLI, agents can now inspect state and perform tasks in milliseconds without going through the simulator. By only sending commands to the simulator in remote mode when needed, UI layout inspection overhead was also eliminated.
fields.sections.7.ko: Shopify has already fully migrated the Shop app to Native, the Shopify app is underway, and the rest will follow soon. However, this process is not simply a language conversion; it redesigns the architecture such that neither performance, stability, accessibility, nor product quality is compromised while also allowing both humans and agents to rapidly understand and make changes. The migration itself is not the end; success will be measured by product speed, app quality, and the volume of autonomous agent work.
fields.sections.8.ko: In 2020, React Native was the right choice for Shopify, and that success was made possible by the efforts of countless engineers and the open source community. The reason Native is the better choice today is that the fundamental premise—the capabilities of coding agents—has changed, illustrating that technology decisions are not absolute but depend on the state of circumstances and tools at the time. The company extends gratitude to Meta's React Native team, the Skia and Reanimated communities, and hundreds of internal engineers, explicitly stating that this transition would not have been possible without their contributions.
fields.caveat: Shopify's experience is tailored to its scale, organization, existing codebase, and level of AI adoption, so before applying it directly to your team or company's technology choices, carefully consider your own context.
